patch.value: Delegate memory credential detection to SDK mutation secret scanner
Implements companion pm-cli-website-d8bz G7. Delegate shared credential grammars to scanMutationSecrets, preserving explicit email consent and narrowly documented stronger memory rules.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Companion pm-cli-website-d8bz is read-only specification. Compare every existing credential rule against the public scanner before removal; retain local email, retention and identity/path policies, with real no-git tracker refusal and allowance tests.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Shared provider credential rules now use scanMutationSecrets. Supplements cover low-entropy and alias assignments, 16-character legacy keys, authorization headers, URL passwords, unbounded JWTs and mixed-case/long private-key markers. Four bounded decoding passes cover encoded/normalized credentials. SDK private-host matching is quadratic on hyphenated noncredentials, so shared scans use overlapping bounded windows with repeated-window reuse; domain path/identity rules retain their scope. See docs/sdk-adoption.md.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Validation: shared SDK scanner/decoding behavioral revert failed all 9 provider/encoded cases; the stronger-supplement corpus separately fails on revert because SDK-only provider credentials would enter memory. Restoration passed 15/15 adoption tests and the supplemental case. Linked scanner tests passed 9/9 with pm test --run --progress; adversarial privacy deadline controls passed 4/4. Production dependency audit found zero vulnerabilities. README, architecture and docs/sdk-adoption.md document the SDK floor, preserved local policies and scanner bounds. Full unchanged coverage/release gates remain CI work.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Post-PR adversarial inspection found a concrete encoded-credential bypass: a malformed UTF-8 suffix caused decodeURIComponent to retain the entire percent run, concealing an otherwise valid credential prefix. Replace invalid bytes in the inspection view instead, preserving valid decoded bytes. Add a real-tracker non-echoing regression and isolated before/fixed proof before the next review push.

Focused malformed/boundary controls passed 3/3, adversarial deadlines 4/4, and linked scanner runs passed 10/10 plus the supplemental corpus. Typecheck, lint, duplication and docstrings pass. This follow-up accompanies the code before the next review push.

value.author: pi-agent
value.text: Review round 7 finding (src/transfer.ts export diagnostic): the bare catch collapses every privacy refusal to 'Credential-shaped memory refused'/'Remove credentials' and converts non-MemoryError defects into a credential refusal. Class rule: a mid-pipeline wrapper around the package's own privacy refusals must preserve the real message and remedy with its added record/field context, and rethrow anything that is not a privacy MemoryError. Both wrap sites live in transfer.ts (export field loop, import sourcePrivacy line scan); fixing both through one shared core.ts helper. Adversarial tests: export refuses stored bodies for each distinct refusal mode (credential-shaped, normalization limit, escaped declaration) asserting the real cause+remedy+record/field context, plus a wrapper property control that rethrows arbitrary non-domain values unchanged.

value.author: pi-agent
value.text: Round-7 fix (thread PRRT_kwDOVPw2oc61NEfw), class rule: a wrapper around the package's own privacy refusals must preserve the real refusal category, message and remedy (adding only its safe context) and rethrow any failure that is not a privacy MemoryError, so defects never masquerade as credential policy. Fixed instances of the class: the export field loop in transfer.ts replaced every thrown value with 'Credential-shaped memory refused'/'Remove credentials' (wrong for the normalization-limit, escaped-declaration and any future privacy cause, and it hid non-MemoryError defects); the import source scan in transfer.ts cast every caught line value to MemoryError without checking. Both now use one shared core.ts helper (privacyRefusal). The class search covered every privacy() call site (commands, SDK paths, import and export, packed npm/bun consumers share the same in-process code): these were the only two wrappers that re-diagnosed a caught value; all other call sites either propagate the refusal or already assert the domain before casting. New adversarial tests: export refusals preserve each real privacy cause and remedy for the exact record and field (credential-shaped, normalization limit, escaped declaration); a wrapper property control that a privacy refusal passes through unchanged and that ordinary errors, TypeError, strings, numbers, null, AggregateError and non-privacy MemoryErrors all rethrow as themselves. docs/sdk-adoption.md documents the preserved-cause contract.

Restoring the wrapper passes both controls.
